title: Procedural generation
summary: Procedural generation is an algorithmic method of creating game content such as levels, textures, and worlds using human-designed rules combined with computer randomness. It enables large, varied game spaces from small codebases by employing deterministic parameters and random seeds. The technique supports replayability but can produce generic output without sufficient human guidance to ensure perceived uniqueness.

mechanisms.title: Deterministic parameter-driven generation
mechanisms.explanation: Content is computed algorithmically from predefined human-authored parameters, allowing consistent recreation of specific worlds or assets when the same seed or parameters are used.

mechanisms.title: Random seed and pseudorandom number generation
mechanisms.explanation: Short seed values initialize pseudorandom number generators to produce large, exchangeable game worlds that appear handcrafted while remaining deterministic and reproducible.
